text:
leah: Heads up — noticed weird hourly tag drift in the billing UI. Last night's preemptible credits seem to have been applied to the wrong team window. Anyone else see the 'tagged_burn' metric jump around 02:00 UTC?
maria: Saw the alert this morning. Cost pipeline shows a big negative adjustment from supplier credits at ~01:50 UTC. Paging @kevin to confirm ingestion/windowing behavior.
kevin: Yep this rings a bell — our transform batches hourly then backfills credits in the next pass, which can move costs into the previous hour. I'll pull the transform job logs now. Do you have a concrete example?
leah: Example: project-redwood-prod shows ~41.2 GPU-hr @ spot for 01:30–02:30, but the charge is attributed to tag 'experimental-sandbox' between 02:00-03:00 in the dashboard. Looks like credit attribution timestamp != consumption window.
sam: If costs shift hours like that it skews team burn dashboards and can trigger alerts. For customer billing we need invoice-level correctness first, but internal dashboards should avoid these hour-level artifacts.
kevin: Quick idea: attribute credits to consumption_window_end rather than the raw credit ingestion timestamp. That would smooth out hour spikes introduced by late-arriving credits. Prototype snippet below:
```
# billing-transform pseudo
if credit.arrival_time < charge.window_end - timedelta(minutes=5):
    attribution_timestamp = charge.window_end
else:
    attribution_timestamp = credit.arrival_time
```
finance-bot: Invoice adjustment created: INV-2026-004 (hold). See finance dashboard -> adjustments.
maria: Can we do this auto-smoothing safely? Proposal: when credit batch timestamp < consumption_window_end by >5m, reassign to consumption_window_end to avoid hour-level drift. What are the risks?
leah: Main risk is for teams that actively monitor real-time hourly burn (experiments, oncall) — they'll see a delayed dip/spike. But for invoicing and weekly budgets it's preferable. Suggest a per-team flag: hour_sensitive = true/false so we can preserve raw timing where needed.
sam: Agree with the per-team flag. Default smoothing ON for internal teams and OFF for customer-facing invoiceable buckets. We should write a short RFC and an ops runbook for the backfill.
kevin: I'll open a PR that adds the attribution rule and a migration script to re-aggregate the last 7 days. Also will update alerting to use a 1-hour moving average to avoid churn.
maria: Finance needs to review the runbook and the backfill plan before we auto-apply changes to production. @kevin drop the PR link and runbook here when ready.
kevin: PR here: https://github.com/redwood/billing/pull/2197 — includes tests and backfill plan. Running local re-agg now, ETA ~35m.
leah: Thanks. Once finance signs off we can merge to staging for one cycle (staging run tomorrow 02:00 UTC). @sam please notify customer-facing teams — they'll see tiny burn reassignments in dashboards for the affected window.
finance-bot: Runbook approval requested: invoice_adj_2026_004. Status: pending finance signoff.
maria: :thumbsup: signed off on the runbook and the 7-day backfill. Please schedule during low-traffic window and add a changelog entry.
kevin: Will schedule and add a changelog. I'll also set the alert dampener for 3 hours around the backfill to avoid noise.
leah: Great — appreciate the quick turnaround. Follow up if the local re-agg surfaces any unexpected tag combos.
kevin: Noted, I'll post results here when re-agg finishes.
